paṃsu:
[Paṃsa+u]  CL=9 1. Earth, soil (mye, myekyi)
2. Dust, fine particles (myehmun, phun, myumhun)
3. Humus, fertile soil (myehsweh, myeoza)
4. Sand (theh)
5. Ashes (specifically cremation ashes - thinchaing pyar)
paṃsati sobhāvi sesaṃ nāsetīti paṃsu, reṇu. ṇvādi, 2.
(pāgu, pā su-saṃ)
The word paṃsu has several meanings in Buddhist contexts:
And as an adjective (paṃsu):
[pa + aṃsu] meaning 'high' or 'elevated'
paṃsuantara: [Paṃsu+antara] (na) CL=8 Between the dust (or) inside the dust.
paṃsucuṇṇaka: [Paṃsu+cuṇṇaka] (na) CL=9 small particle of earth ( fine earth (or) a very very small part of earth like dust), Dust.
paṃsudhota: [Paṃsu+dhota]  CL=9 'That which has been cleaned/cleared of dust and dirt' or 'freed from dust and impurities'
paṃsudhovaka: [Paṃsu+dhovaka] (ti) CL=8 clean and clear dust; he.
paṃsudhovakantevāsī: [Paṃsudhovaka+antevāsī] (ti) CL=10 disciple of him who cleaned and cleared dust. Paṃsudhovaka - Look.
paṃsudhovakasutta: [Paṃsudhovaka+sutta] (na) CL=8 Paṃsudhovaka  Sutta (or) Sutta named Paṃsudhovaka.
paṃsugata: [Paṃsu+gata] (ti) CL=8 be dirty all over with dust .

paṃsuguhā: [Paṃsu+guhā] (thī) CL=8 earth cave (or) cave made by earth/land, earth tomb (or) tomb made by earth/land.

paṃsuhāraka: [Paṃsu+hāraka] (ti) CL=8 Who took the land; he.

paṃsukīḷita: [Paṃsu+kīḷita] (ti) CL=8 Who play with dust; dusty playmate; dusty playfellow.
paṃsukūla:
[Paṃsu+kūla]  CL=8 (1) Cloth discarded on the ground. (2) Ownerless items/objects. (3) Paṃsukūla robe. paṃsukūla (n) [paṃsukūla+dhāraṇa. dhāraṇa word omitted.] Wearing-carrying-bearing of paṃsukūla robe.
See also paṃsukūlika.The elevation of earth. See the bracket below.
paṃsukūla (n) [paṃsukūla+a. paṃsu+ku+ula+a. rathikasusānasaṅkārakūṭādīnaṃ yattha katthaci paṃsūnaṃ upari ṭhitattā abbhuggatṭṭhena tesu tesu paṃsukūlamivāti paṃsukūlaṃ, atha vā paṃsu viya kucchitabhāvaṃ ulatīti paṃsukūlaṃ, kucchitabhāvaṃ gacchatīti vuttaṃ hoti. Visuddhimagga,1.57. paṃsu viya kucchitaṃ ulati pavatatīti vā paṃsukūlaṃ. Visuddhimagga,Ṭīkā,1.89. See also paṃsukūlikaṅga.]
